code_review.fix_description: Replaced unconditional Math.ceil() with parseFloat(...toFixed(2)) for order_amount in both placeOrder (L382) and updateCustomerOrder (L531)
code_review.fix_rationale: When restaurant has total_round='No' and total is fractional (e.g. ₹1.26), Math.ceil was sending order_amount:2 instead of 1.26, overcharging customers. The fix passes the exact value from ReviewOrder which already handles rounding based on total_round setting.
code_review.backward_compatibility: Fix preserves correct behavior for total_round='Yes' restaurants because ReviewOrder already ceils the value before passing it

context_for_next_testing_agent: BUG-2026-10-25-002 fix verified via code inspection. Both edits in orderService.ts confirmed at L382 and L531. The fix replaces Math.ceil with parseFloat toFixed(2) for order_amount field. End-to-end testing of fractional order amounts would require a restaurant with total_round='No' and items with fractional prices - this is a POS configuration that may not be available on preprod.
rca_of_the_issue: orderService.ts was unconditionally applying Math.ceil() to order_amount at L381 (placeOrder) and L529 (updateCustomerOrder). This caused fractional totals like ₹1.26 to be sent as ₹2 to POS, overcharging customers when restaurant had total_round='No'. The fix passes the already-rounded value from ReviewOrder (which respects the restaurant's total_round setting) using parseFloat toFixed(2) instead of Math.ceil.
